title: Quality gates Console experience: gate results, failure states, and override confirmation UX
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Design the Console UX for viewing quality gate results for Optimize config changes, including:
- clear pass/fail/pending states, with actionable reasons
- warnings + blocked “Apply” behavior when gates fail
- override request + override confirmation flows (time-bound, audited)
- copy guidelines for customer-facing text and admin-only controls

Context
Optimize can suggest/apply cost-saving config changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles). This ticket defines the Console experience for quality gating before changes can be applied to production traffic.

Primary users / personas
1) App owner (self-serve): wants one-click apply; needs quick “is it safe?” summary, minimal jargon.
2) Platform / ML engineer (enterprise): wants artifacts, deltas vs baseline, reproducibility, audit trail.
3) Oncall / SRE: needs fast triage paths for failures/timeouts; needs to distinguish regressions vs eval flakiness.
4) Approver (admin/enterprise): can grant time-bound override; needs warnings + policy reminders.

Information architecture (Console)
A) Optimize Recommendation detail panel (where user sees cost savings suggestion)
- New “Quality gates” section with:
  - Status chip: Pending | Running | Passed | Failed | Overridden | Expired | Not required
  - Gate tier label: Smoke gate | Full gate (if available)
  - “View results” link (always present when gate exists)
  - “Why is this blocked?” inline explanation for Failed/Running/Timeout
- Apply button rules:
  - Passed: Apply enabled
  - Running/Pending: Apply disabled; tooltip “Waiting for quality evaluation to finish”
  - Failed: Apply disabled; error summary + link to results
  - Overridden: Apply enabled, but requires confirmation modal and displays expiration
  - Not required: Apply enabled (policy-driven; shown as “Not required by policy”) with link to policy details

B) Gate Results page (drill-down)
Entry points:
- “View results” from Recommendation detail
- Gate run ID link from activity/audit log

Layout
1) Header: “Quality gate results” + run ID + environment + route/model + timestamp
2) Summary card:
- Outcome (Passed/Failed/Overridden/Timed out)
- Baseline vs Proposed config (diff view)
- Key deltas: overall quality delta, rubric/task metrics deltas, confidence level / variance note
- Eval metadata: prompt set(s), sample size, eval-harness version, gate tier
3) Details tabs (MVP: collapsed sections; v1: tabs)
- Metrics: table showing metric name, baseline, proposed, delta, threshold, pass/fail indicator
- Failures: list of “failed checks” with human-readable reasons
- Artifacts: links to logs, per-prompt outputs, trace IDs, and “download bundle” (if supported)
- Retries / flakiness: rerun count, flake score (if available), quarantine notice if prompt set quarantined
4) Actions panel (right rail)
- Request override (if eligible)
- Rerun gate (if allowed by policy; MVP: limited to internal/admin)
- Copy links: “Copy run link”, “Copy diff”

State mapping (must match state machine)
- pending: created but not yet enqueued
- running: eval in progress
- passed: all required checks passed
- failed: one or more required checks failed
- overridden: override granted; includes expiration + approver
- canceled: canceled by user/system; treated as blocked
- timed_out: treated as blocked; show guidance to rerun or contact support
- expired: override expired; treated as blocked until a new gate passes or new override granted

Copy: user-visible strings (draft)
Status chips
- Pending: “Queued” (tooltip: “Evaluation is queued. Apply will be available after the gate completes.”)
- Running: “Running” (tooltip: “Evaluation in progress. This usually takes 10–25 minutes.”)
- Passed: “Passed”
- Failed: “Failed”
- Overridden: “Override granted”
- Expired: “Override expired”
- Not required: “Not required by policy”

Blocked apply banner (Failed)
Title: “Can’t apply: quality gate failed”
Body: “This change didn’t meet the required quality thresholds. Review the failing checks and artifacts before making changes.”
Primary link: “View results”
Secondary link: “Request override” (only if policy allows)

Blocked apply banner (Running)
Title: “Apply is disabled while evaluation runs”
Body: “We’re evaluating quality impact for this change. You can leave this page—results will be saved to the run.”

Timed out
Title: “Evaluation timed out”
Body: “The evaluation didn’t finish within the allowed time window. You can retry, or contact support if this persists.”
Button: “Retry evaluation” (if allowed)

Override request flow (policy-driven)
Entry points:
- “Request override” from Results page or Recommendation detail when failed/blocked

Step 1: Request form (modal)
- Title: “Request time-bound override”
- Body: “Overrides allow applying changes that did not meet quality thresholds. Overrides are audited and expire automatically.”
- Required fields:
  - Expiration: “Expires in” dropdown (24h, 72h, 7d) with policy-based max
  - Justification: text area (min 80 chars)
  - Evidence: link(s) input (optional but strongly encouraged; policy can require)
- Footer:
  - Primary: “Submit request”
  - Secondary: “Cancel”

Step 2: Confirmation (after submission)
- Title: “Override request submitted”
- Body: “An approver will review your request. You can track status in the activity log.”
- Link: “View request in activity”

Override grant confirmation (approver)
Modal shown when approver clicks “Grant override”
- Title: “Grant override to apply a failed change?”
- Warning callout:
  - “This change failed quality gates and may degrade outputs in production. Overrides are time-bound and audited.”
- Required inputs:
  - Expiration (default + max enforced)
  - Approver note (required)
- Primary: “Grant override”
- Secondary: “Cancel”

Override applied confirmation (requester applying under override)
When user clicks Apply with “Override granted” status
- Title: “Apply under override?”
- Body: “This change is being applied under an active override (expires {date/time}). This action will be recorded in audit logs.”
- Checkbox: “I understand this may impact output quality” (required)
- Primary: “Apply change”
- Secondary: “Cancel”

Audit trail UI (Console activity)
Add activity timeline entries:
- “Gate started” / “Gate completed” (Pass/Fail/Timeout)
- “Override requested” + requester + justification snippet
- “Override granted” + approver + expiration
- “Override expired”
- “Change applied” + whether under override
Each entry links to:
- gate run details
- config diff
- artifacts (if permitted)

Accessibility + safety notes
- All status information must be conveyed beyond color (text + icon + accessible label)
- Error copy avoids blame; provides next steps
- Avoid leaking prompt content to users without permission; artifacts link should respect RBAC
- Enterprise: show “Export audit event” / “View in audit log” deep link when available

Instrumentation (requested by PM/Eng)
Track these events (names TBD by telemetry team):
- gate_results_viewed
- apply_blocked_due_to_gate (include reason: failed/running/timeout/expired)
- override_requested
- override_granted
- apply_under_override_confirmed

Open questions / decisions
- Rerun policy: MVP recommends showing “Retry evaluation” only for internal/admin; for customers, link to support if repeated timeouts.
- “Not required by policy” display: keep visible to reduce confusion; include ‘why’ link to policy docs.
- Flaky eval messaging: if flake score high or prompt set quarantined, show “Results may be unreliable” and block apply until rerun with stable suite (policy).

Deliverables
- Finalized UX flow spec (states + screens)
- Copy deck (strings above) for eng integration
- Component guidance (status chip, banners, modals)
- Handoff notes for ENG-3925 (Console) + ENG-3927 (audit events)

Links
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd.json
- System design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-quality-gates-system-design.json
- Override policy: sources/confluence/policies-and-process/change-management/exception-policy-optimize-quality-gate-overrides.json
- Console UX notes (early): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/console-ux-quality-gate-results-wire-notes.json

Acceptance criteria
- Console blocks Apply when gate state is Failed/Running/Pending/Timed out/Expired.
- Console shows a persistent “Quality gates” section with a status chip and a working “View results” entry point.
- Results page communicates: what changed (diff), what was evaluated (prompt sets/suite), how it compared (baseline vs proposed), and why it passed/failed (failed checks + thresholds).
- Override experience is time-bound, explicit, and includes confirmation warnings for both approver and applier.
- Copy is consistent across recommendation panel, results page, and activity log.
- Handoff includes exact strings and state mapping for engineering implementation.
comments: 2025-11-20 — Aditya Rao (PM): Please keep the recommendation detail view lightweight. Most users should not need to interpret raw metric tables unless they click through. Also confirm which states are MVP vs v1; we can ship Results page as MVP, but tabs can wait.

2025-11-22 — Dylan Brooks (Console Eng): We can implement a status chip + banner + ‘View results’ with existing layout components. For the Results page, please specify the minimum fields required from the API (run id, state, top-level pass/fail reasons, artifact pointers).

2025-11-25 — Jordan Lee (Policy/Enforcement): Ensure UI supports ‘Not required by policy’ for some routes/tiers; we don’t want users to think gating is broken when policy exempts. Also, expired overrides must re-block apply even if the prior run is still visible.

2025-11-27 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add a distinct timeout state and copy that pushes users to retry first, then support if persistent. We’re seeing region capacity issues during spikes and don’t want this to look like a quality regression.

2025-12-02 — Karthik Iyer (Applied ML): Include a clear ‘failing checks’ list. Avoid showing statistical jargon by default; keep confidence/variance language behind an info tooltip so we don’t confuse non-ML users.

2025-12-04 — Paula Mendes (PM): Override confirmation must be explicit. Approver needs a required note + expiration; applier needs a checkbox acknowledgement. Also we should show override expiration prominently near the Apply button.

2025-12-08 — Marcus Lin (Security): Artifacts links must respect RBAC. If a user lacks permission, show ‘You don’t have access to artifacts for this run’ instead of a broken link. Also confirm audit trail text doesn’t leak prompt content.

2026-01-07 — Chloe Martin (Console Backend): Proposed API will return a summary object and artifact ids/urls. We can support ‘Copy run link’ and deep links from activity entries. Please finalize the exact status chip labels to keep them stable for docs.
updates: 2025-11-26 — Kenji Nakamura: Drafted core flows for recommendation detail + results page + override request/grant/apply. Sharing copy for review in this ticket; will align state names with ENG-3921 state machine.

2025-12-05 — Kenji Nakamura: Incorporated PM/SRE feedback: added timeout/expired states, reduced default statistical language, added explicit override confirmation checkbox. Marking ready for eng handoff pending API field confirmation.
2025-12-10 — Kenji Nakamura: Handoff sent to ENG-3925 with required API fields and final copy set. Remaining follow-up: verify artifact permission handling text with Security.
2026-01-09 — Kenji Nakamura: Closed after final security copy adjustments (RBAC-friendly artifact messaging) and alignment with override expiration rules from PM-482.
